localBiteReport: The most current verifiable report with Choctawhatchee Bay-specific inshore detail is from the week of September 4–10, 2026 — roughly 10 days old, not this current week. According to Captain Blake Nelson of Last Cast Charters (Choctawhatchee Bay), the bay is showing early signs of the fall transition, with large concentrations of bait — pogies and greenies — moving from open water into bayous, bridge areas, and flats. Bull redfish and jack crevalle are actively feeding on those bait schools around Rocky Bayou, Boggy Bayou, Joe's Bayou, Marler Bayou, and near the East Pass, best targeted on topwater plugs and large swimbaits. Slot reds, speckled trout, and mangrove snapper are holding around grass edges, sandy pockets, docks, and deeper cuts; afternoon thunderstorms have been the primary safety concern for anglers on the bay. Looking ahead, Blake expected the first meaningful slot-redfish push tied to the fall mullet run to begin during the second or third week of September — which aligns with this week — making now a potentially prime transition window. Water temperature at this location is 87°F.
